title: Precision dynamics of resonantly enhanced optical parametric amplifiers
abstract: Optical parametric amplification is a crucial technology for the production of continuous-wave squeezed vacuum, which is now applied to gravitational-wave interferometry and other highly sensitive measurements of optical phase. The amplifiers employed in gravitational-wave detection are resonantly enhanced with optical cavities, which introduces nontrivial dynamics to their operation and requires a frequency-domain model of the relations between optical fields. In this work, input-output relations between optical fields entering, circulating in, and exiting a model amplifier are solved directly to produce frequency-domain relations that fully incorporate the cavity dynamics. We also provide low-order zero-pole-gain expansions for these relations to facilitate their analysis from a feedback control perspective. In the limit of small cavity decay rates, our relations are shown to reduce to relations previously derived under a Hamiltonian formalism. Expressions for amplifier figures of merit and for squeezed quadrature variances are also analyzed. Along the way, we examine how information about the amplifier performance can be extracted from the frequency dependence of the input-output relations, providing characterization methods that are complementary to methods that examine the static amplifier behavior.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous frequency-domain model for optical parametric amplifiers integrated into resonant cavities, crucial for applications like gravitational-wave detectors. By solving input-output relations directly, the authors capture full cavity dynamics, providing advanced characterization methods beyond static analyses. This advances the theoretical toolkit for modeling quantum light sources in high-finesse optical systems.
main_problem: The work develops a comprehensive frequency-domain model for resonantly enhanced optical parametric amplifiers (OPAs) that fully incorporates complex cavity dynamics, moving beyond simpler Hamiltonian formalisms.
main_result: The direct input-output relation approach yields frequency-dependent transfer functions that provide complementary characterization methods compared to static measurements of amplifier performance.
method: The authors solve the input-output relations directly in the frequency domain by modeling field propagation through the cavity, and they derive low-order zero-pole-gain expansions for analysis.
model_or_system: The physical system is an OPA used in gravitational-wave interferometry, where the amplifier is coupled to an optical cavity. The model tracks input, circulating, and output optical fields using frequency-domain transfer functions.
key_observables: Input–output relations (transfer functions), amplifier figures of merit, squeezed quadrature variances, and frequency dependence of these relations.
important_parameters: Cavity decay rates, free spectral range effects, and the detuning parameters ($\Phi_a, \Phi_b$) governing resonance conditions.
main_assumptions: The analysis compares results derived from a direct field-tracking method against those from standard Hamiltonian formalisms, noting that the direct method is necessary to capture finite free spectral range dynamics.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the resonant OPA setup detailing various optical paths and coupling elements; other figures likely show frequency dependence plots of transfer functions or gain.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the necessity of a full cavity model, deriving the input-output relations in the frequency domain, providing low-order expansions for control analysis, analyzing key performance metrics, and comparing results to established Hamiltonian formalisms.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles open quantum systems dynamics (OPAs) by developing advanced theoretical tools (frequency-domain transfer functions) necessary for modeling high-precision quantum measurements like gravitational wave detection.
